answer: Seats in this registry are not free names but shares sold out of a shallow pool. Every membership burns one share, and the burn permanently deepens the floor: the next price is the pool ratio, so a farm buying k seats pays roughly k-squared halves of the opening price and cannot refund its way back to the old level. An orchard of clones therefore grows dearer with every branch, the pigment of wealth stops stretching, and the trellis of honest members stays the cheap foothold. Waiting does not help, because the floor never falls.
